title: CloudFront distributions, origins, and cache behaviors
hook: A CloudFront distribution is the configuration object that ties your domain name to one or more origins and the rules that decide which origin handles each URL path.

blocks.text: An Amazon CloudFront distribution has a unique domain (d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net or your alternate domain name), one or more origins (where content lives), and an ordered list of cache behaviors. Each behavior matches a path pattern (for example /api/*), selects an origin, and defines TTL, compression, allowed HTTP methods, and which headers/query strings/cookies participate in caching. The default behavior (path pattern *) catches everything not matched above — order matters: most specific patterns first.

blocks.text: Misconfigured behaviors are the root cause of most CloudFront production incidents: API traffic cached like static files, wrong origin because Host header was not forwarded, or SPA routes returning S3 AccessDenied instead of index.html. Senior engineers design behaviors as a routing table — static long TTL, API zero TTL, default shell for client routing — and attach AWS WAF at the distribution for edge security.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Draw three behaviors: /assets/* → S3, /api/* → ALB, default * → S3 index.html. Mention custom error responses for 403/404 → 200 /index.html.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: TLS terminates at edge
items.body: Viewer connects to nearest PoP with your ACM certificate (must be in us-east-1 for CloudFront).

items.title: Match path to behavior
items.body: CloudFront evaluates behaviors top to bottom; first matching pattern wins.

items.title: Apply cache policy
items.body: Cache policy defines TTL bounds and what goes into the cache key (managed or custom).

items.title: Forward to origin on miss
items.body: Origin request policy controls which headers, cookies, and query strings reach ALB or S3.

diagram.title: Behavior routing

snippet.label: CLI — list distributions and get config
snippet.code:
aws cloudfront list-distributions \
  --query 'DistributionList.Items[*].[Id,DomainName,Status]' \
  --output table

aws cloudfront get-distribution-config \
  --id E1234567890ABC \
  --output json > dist-config.json
snippet.explanation: get-distribution-config returns ETag required for updates. Inspect Origins and CacheBehaviors.Items ordering — behaviors are evaluated in array order.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — multi-origin distribution with behaviors
snippet.code:
Resources:
  WebDistribution:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::Distribution
    Properties:
      DistributionConfig:
        Enabled: true
        Aliases:
          - app.example.com
        ViewerCertificate:
          AcmCertificateArn: !Ref AppCert
          SslSupportMethod: sni-only
          MinimumProtocolVersion: TLSv1.2_2021
        Origins:
          - Id: S3Static
            DomainName: !GetAtt StaticBucket.RegionalDomainName
            OriginAccessControlId: !GetAtt StaticOAC.Id
          - Id: ApiAlb
            DomainName: !GetAtt AppAlb.DNSName
            CustomOriginConfig:
              HTTPSPort: 443
              OriginProtocolPolicy: https-only
        CacheBehaviors:
          - PathPattern: '/api/*'
            TargetOriginId: ApiAlb
            ViewerProtocolPolicy: https-only
            AllowedMethods: [GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE]
            CachePolicyId: 4135ea2d-6df8-44a3-9df3-4b5a84be39ad  # CachingDisabled
            OriginRequestPolicyId: b689b0a8-53d0-40ab-baf2-68738e2966ac  # AllViewer
        DefaultCacheBehavior:
          TargetOriginId: S3Static
          ViewerProtocolPolicy: redirect-to-https
          CachePolicyId: 658327ea-f89d-4fab-a63d-7e88639e58f6  # CachingOptimized
        CustomErrorResponses:
          - ErrorCode: 403
            ResponseCode: 200
            ResponsePagePath: /index.html
            ErrorCachingMinTTL: 10
          - ErrorCode: 404
            ResponseCode: 200
            ResponsePagePath: /index.html
            ErrorCachingMinTTL: 10
snippet.explanation: /api/* uses CachingDisabled and AllViewer so ALB sees Host and Authorization. Default serves SPA from S3. Custom errors map S3 missing keys to index.html for React Router.

snippet.label: CLI — attach WAF Web ACL to distribution
snippet.explanation: WAF for CloudFront must be created in us-east-1 (global scope). Blocks bots and geo traffic before origin.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — origin group failover
snippet.code:
OriginGroups:
  - Id: S3FailoverGroup
    FailoverCriteria:
      StatusCodes:
        StatusCodes: [500, 502, 503, 504]
        Quantity: 4
    Members:
      - OriginId: S3Primary
      - OriginId: S3Secondary
DefaultCacheBehavior:
  TargetOriginId: S3FailoverGroup
  # ... cache policy etc.
snippet.explanation: Origin group tries secondary S3 bucket when primary returns 5xx. Useful for static DR; APIs usually use Route 53 health checks instead.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Putting default * behavior before /api/* — order is wrong so API never matches. Forgetting ACM certificate in us-east-1 for custom domains. Using S3 REST endpoint as origin without OAC while bucket is private. Not forwarding Host to ALB — ALB listener rules never match.

blocks.text: Managed cache and origin request policies replaced legacy forwarded-values — prefer AWS managed IDs (CachingOptimized, CachingDisabled, AllViewer) unless you need a custom cache key. Continuous deployment: use CloudFormation or Terraform with ETag on update-distribution; drift from console edits causes surprise. How to prove it in production: enable standard logging, sample x-host-header and sc-status; test each path pattern with curl -H 'Host: app.example.com'. Origin connection attempts and 502s often mean wrong origin domain or SSL protocol mismatch.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Custom auth keys need custom policy

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Describing a distribution as 'just DNS to S3' without behaviors, origins, or TLS. Strong answer: ordered path behaviors, separate cache policies for static vs API, custom errors for SPA, WAF at viewer.

interviewTakeaways: A distribution maps URLs to origins via ordered cache behaviors; the default * behavior is the fallback.
ACM certificates for CloudFront custom domains must live in us-east-1; behaviors need distinct cache policies for static vs API.
Production tip: enable access logs and alarm on 5xx ratio; test /api/* with Authorization forwarded.
60s: Distribution = domain + origins + behaviors. Specific paths first. API TTL 0 + AllViewer. SPA custom errors. WAF at edge.
Follow-up: when would you split into two distributions instead of one?
commonPitfalls: Wrong behavior order — saying '/api is cached' because default behavior caught it first gets you rejected.
Strong answer: draw behavior table with path, origin, cache policy, and forwarded headers.
Custom domain without us-east-1 ACM certificate.
ALB origin returns 502 because OriginProtocolPolicy is http-only but ALB only listens on 443.

jsTsCorrelations.note: app.use('/api', apiRouter) plus express.static mirrors CloudFront /api/* and default behaviors. CloudFront adds global edge; Express runs in one region.
Angular build output puts hashed files under /browser/ or assets/. CloudFront /assets/* behavior must match your deploy folder structure or deep links 404.
